text: For this reason we must pay much closer attention to what we have heard, so that we do not drift away.

versions.text: For this reason we must pay all the closer attention to what we have heard, so that we do not drift away.
versions.explanation: "pay all the closer attention" is archaic and stumbles when read aloud; "much closer attention" renders περισσοτέρως naturally and keeps the rhythm.

text: For if the word spoken through angels proved binding, and every transgression and act of disobedience received its just penalty,
how shall we escape if we neglect so great a salvation? It was declared at first by the Lord, and confirmed to us by those who heard him,
while God bore witness along with them by signs and wonders and various miracles, and by gifts of the Holy Spirit distributed according to his will.
For it was not to angels that God subjected the world to come, of which we are speaking.
But someone has testified somewhere: "What is man, that you remember him, or the son of man, that you care for him?
You made him for a little while lower than the angels; you crowned him with glory and honor,
putting everything in subjection under his feet." Now in subjecting all things to him, God left nothing outside his control. Yet at present we do not see everything subjected to him.
But we do see Jesus, who was made for a little while lower than the angels, now crowned with glory and honor because he suffered death, so that by the grace of God he might taste death for everyone.
For it was fitting that God, for whom and through whom all things exist, in bringing many sons to glory, should make the pioneer of their salvation perfect through suffering.
For the one who sanctifies and those who are sanctified all have the same origin. That is why he is not ashamed to call them brothers,
saying, "I will proclaim your name to my brothers; in the midst of the congregation I will sing your praise."
And again, "I will put my trust in him." And again, "Here I am, and the children God has given me."

Since, then, the children share in flesh and blood, he himself likewise shared fully in the same, so that through death he might break the power of the one who holds the power of death—that is, the devil—

versions.text: Since, then, the children share in flesh and blood, he too shared the same humanity, so that through death he might break the power of the one who holds the power of death—that is, the devil—
versions.explanation: παραπλησίως ("in like manner, likewise") is not represented, and "the same humanity" narrows the Greek τῶν αὐτῶν ("the same things," i.e. flesh and blood). The revision keeps the emphasis on his full identification with the children.

text: and set free all those who through fear of death were held in slavery all their lives.
For surely it is not angels he helps, but the descendants of Abraham.
Therefore he had to be made like his brothers in every respect, so that he might become a merciful and faithful high priest in the service of God, to make atonement for the sins of the people.
For he himself suffered when he was tempted, and so he is able to help those who are being tempted.

versions.text: For because he himself suffered when he was tempted, he is able to help those who are being tempted.
versions.explanation: "For because" stacks two conjunctions and is awkward to read aloud; a single causal conjunction carries the sense of the Greek clearly.

versions.text: Because he himself suffered when he was tempted, he is able to help those who are being tempted.
versions.explanation: The Greek γάρ links this sentence back to verse 17, explaining why the Son had to be made like his brothers. Rendering it as "Because" turns the connective inward and loses the tie to the preceding verse. "For ... and so" keeps both the link to verse 17 and the internal cause-and-result, and it reads smoothly aloud. The present reading is a defensible rendering of the causal force.
